:::{#def-poisson-regression}
#### Poisson regression model

Let $Y$ be a count [outcome](https://morrison-lab.github.io/sds/model-validation.html#def-outcome-vector),
$\vX$ a [covariate vector](correlation-regression.qmd#def-slr-covariate-vector),
and $T$ the [exposure magnitude](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/distributions.html#def-exposure)
over which the [events](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/probability-basics.html#def-event) in $Y$ are counted.
A **Poisson regression model** assumes that,
given $\vX = \vx$ and $T = t$,
$Y$ has a [Poisson distribution](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/distributions.html#def-poisson)
with [mean](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/expectation.html#def-expectation) $\mu(\vx, t) = \lambda(\vx) \cdot t$,
where the [event rate](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/distributions.html#def-event-rate) $\lambda(\vx)$
has a [log](https://morrison-lab.github.io/mds/algebra-exponentials.html#def-natural-log) that is a [linear function](https://morrison-lab.github.io/mds/algebra-exponentials.html#def-linear-function) of the [covariates](model-validation.qmd#def-covariate):

$$
\lnf{\lambda(\vx)} = \beta_0 + \beta_1 x_1 + \dots + \beta_p x_p.
$$

:::
